author: BBC News
description:
Iran says it has agreed a shipping route with Oman in the Strait of Hormuz that could pave the way for the vital waterway to reopen.

It follows more military threats from US President Donald Trump, if Iran doesn’t agree to a deal for free passage.
 
Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi rebels say they have attacked a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea, while Israel has conducted strikes in southern Lebanon, accusing Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire. 
 
And inside Iran, the UN say 56 people have been executed since mid-March on charges relating to national security.

Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Dan Johnson in Kyiv.

description:
Russian drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian targets have ramped up in recent months, as Ukrainian air defences are increasingly tested. 

At least 17 people were killed in the Kyiv region overnight in a large-scale attack, with dozens more injured. 

But did you know many of the weapons inflicting the damage include components made in Western countries including the US, UK and Germany? 

The Security Brief's Mikey Kay, a former Senior Officer in the British Military, explains.

author: BBC News
description:
Two years to the day after resigning as prime minister of Bangladesh, Sheikh Hasina has delivered an address vowing to return home from exile in India. 

The former leader was ousted amid mass protests in 2024, and subsequently sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity. A Bangladeshi court ruled that she had authorised security forces to use "lethal weapons" against protestors. The United Nations has said up to 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.

After her speech, the Bangladeshi Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a statement saying it was "outraged" that Ms Hasina was "allowed ... to engage in live interaction with the media in New Delhi, where she and her henchmen launched venomous vitriol against the State of Bangladesh and her people."

We ask the BBC's South Asia specialist Anbarasan Ethirajan why Ms Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh now, and what could happen if she does. 

Plus, we discuss how the new government of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman -
title: Why ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina may return from India to face a death sentence | Global News Podcast

author: BBC News
description:
A group of prominent, controversial influencers made a visit to Russia this summer.

They included Andrew Tate, Candace Owens and British far-right anti-Islam activist Tommy Robinson. They argue that Russia is upholding the traditional conservative values they fear are in decline at home.

It is certainly an image Vladimir Putin is keen to project. Two years ago Russia set up a special “shared values” visa, which makes it easier for Westerners to move to the country if they align with its supposed ‘traditional spiritual and moral beliefs’.

Russia claims thousands of Westerners have applied.

We speak to the BBC’s Dan Hardoon, whose documentary ‘The Russian Dream’ follows Westerners who have moved to Russia, and to Russia expert Mark Galeotti, host of the podcast In Moscow's Shadows.

description:
Today, there has been more criticism from victims’ families over plans to release some prisoners early.

Under the policy, due to begin in October, thousands of prisoners will be eligible to be released part way through their sentences. Ministers announced last night that prisoners guilty of rape, serious child sex offences and grooming will be excluded. Adam is joined by home and legal affairs correspondent Dominic Casciani and Pia Sinha former prison governor and chief executive of the Prison Reform Trust.

And, after a humbling few days for President Trump is he able to reclaim the initiative before the US midterm elections? Adam is joined by Americast’s Anthony Zurcher.

description:
Part of a SpaceX rocket hurtling towards the Moon is thought to have made impact.
 
The Falcon 9 rocket was launched last year - its 4,000kg upper stage was shed in space, as planned, but went on to be in an accidental collision course with the lunar surface.
 
The crash will be confirmed by specialist telescopes monitoring the event.

description:
Russia has attacked Ukraine with ballistic missiles and drones, killing at least 17 people, as Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said interceptors "could have saved lives".

In one of the deadliest strikes across Kyiv this year - which started after midnight on Wednesday - at least 44 people were injured after residential buildings, a railway station and warehouses were hit, Zelensky said.

The Russia defence ministry said it had struck logistics hubs and supply centres in Kyiv and the surrounding region.

author: BBC News
description:
A new fund is working to save 100 of the world's most threatened species. 

The Phoenix Species Project will put $200m (£149m) towards restoring animals in the wild and stopping them from going extinct. It's one of the largest funds ever focused on species recovery. 

The project is a collaboration between the Bezos Earth Fund and Re:wild - a non profit co-founded by actor Leonardo DiCaprio. 

It comes at a time when conservationists have warned about a decline in global biodiversity, and just a few weeks after the Trump administration rolled back endangered species protections.
